observations:
Torah #21 produces 3 packages from 37 bechina edges across 49 nodes. After thorough gap analysis of the source text, no cluster of 3+ concepts using explicit bechina language was found that forms an independent conceptual domain unaccounted for by the 3 existing packages.

The candidates considered for new packages were:

(1) EVIL-BRAIN CLUSTER (מחין דקטנות, דינים, כעס): The text does explicitly link these three via bechina language — 'דינים הם מחין דקטנות' and 'כעס הוא מחסרון הדעת'. This trio could qualify as an evil Package B mirror. However, examination of the text reveals that the Rebbe treats this as a brief explanatory aside (one paragraph, lines 76-77) embedded within the larger דעת discussion. The text does not develop an independent structure for this cluster the way it does for the 3 main packages. The evil-brain cluster is the diminished form of Package B, not an independent conceptual domain. Recommended resolution: add מחין-דקטנות, דינים, and כעס as evil-polarity bechina edges into the dataset (see additions file), and flag them as Package B evil-mirror additions rather than a new package. If future analysis finds more evil-brain nodes in other Torahs, a cross-Torah evil-brain package could be warranted.

(2) MOURNING/HALITZAH CLUSTER (שבעת ימי אבלות, קריעה, רוק החליצה, בשת פנים): The text discusses halitzah (lines 24-26), mourning (lines 23, 97), and shame (lines 26, 39) at some length. However, these are treated as illustrations of the central שבעת-הנרות / אור-הפנים themes, not as an independent conceptual domain. The bechina language used is: שבעת ימי אבלות = שבעת הנרות (a node already in Package A), and קריעה = שע"נ נהורין = אור הפנים (also Package A). The mourning/halitzah content is subsumed into the Package A structure.

(3) DAAT / ETERNAL LIFE CLUSTER (דעת, חיים נצחיים, גאלה, נחמה): The second half of Torah #21 (sections 11 onward, 'נחמו נחמו') is rich with דעת language. However, the edges coded for these concepts in the dataset (reference=21) are nearly all eitza type ('דעת → גאלה', 'כשנשלם הדעת → נשלם החסרונות'), not bechina. In the source text itself, the Rebbe says 'כי עיקר הגאלה על ידי הדעת' — this is causal (eitza), not a bechina of shared nature. The only bechina usage in this section is 'דעת = מקיפין' (implicitly, since שפע-אלקי = מקיפין = דעת), but this connection runs through Package A nodes already. No independent new domain.

(4) WOMB/IBUR CLUSTER: יבום, גלגול, רחם-אם are mentioned in the text as legal/mystical consequences of the ibur-gestation concept. But these are not given bechina equalities in the source — they are narrative illustrations of what happens when the 7-lights are absent. No bechina cluster forms here.

Conclusion: Torah #21 is structurally a 3-package Torah. The packages are: (A) the divine-influx/מקיפין universe [23 nodes], (B) the human-brain/menorah-of-head universe [17 nodes], (C) the concealment-gestation-birth cycle [9 nodes]. The Torah's argument moves from A (what שפע-אלקי is) → via B (through what organs it enters) → through C (what happens when it is hidden and how it is born again) → back to A (through crying and sanctifying the 7 candles). No additional independent bechina domain was identified.
